- Services gross margin of 75.4% versus products at about 36.8% makes mix the durable margin engine; product gross margin improved to about 40.1% in Q3 FY2026 from 34.5% a year earlier, mostly on mix plus the refund [S1][S6]
- Free cash flow is compounding again: $136.7bn TTM versus $98.8bn in FY2025 (+38%), conversion 1.06x net income versus 0.88x, with capex falling to $10.0bn TTM from $12.7bn - there is no AI datacentre step-up in Apple's capex [S6][S1]
- Capital returns slowed into strength: buybacks $82.2bn TTM versus $90.7bn in FY2025, while net cash rose to $62.2bn from $33.8bn [S6][S1]
- Greater China fell from $72.6bn (FY2023) to $64.4bn (FY2025) then rebounded +22% to $18.8bn in Q3 FY2026 and +30% for the nine months, helped by a stronger renminbi and Pro mix [S1][S6]; IDC shows Apple units down 4.3% in calendar Q3 2026 even as share rose to 17.8% from 15.8% [S18]
- Component cost is the key variable: Apple says memory (DRAM/NAND) and advanced-semiconductor constraints will intensify; each 100bp of gross margin is $0.26 of EPS, or 3.0% of TTM EPS of $8.72, and the guided 200-300bp step-down is worth 6-9% of annual EPS [S6][S24]
- Valuation is at a record: 39.4x TTM P/E on a $5,017.9bn market cap and $4,955.7bn EV, versus a 22.0x Microsoft/Alphabet median (+79%) and a FY2022-FY2025 year-end range of 24.6x-37.5x; EV/Sales is 10.6x versus 6.1x in FY2022 [S7][S9][S11][S1]
- Forward multiple offers no relief: nine-month EPS of $6.88 plus a $1.99 Q4 estimate gives about $8.87 for FY2026, or 38.8x; 60 analysts carry a consensus target of $339.35, 2.1% below the price [S6][S25][S23][S7]
- Services faces regulatory erosion: the EU fined Apple EUR 500m under the DMA, Apple overhauled EU App Store fees in August 2026 under threat of periodic penalties, and a US court order bars commissions on certain purchases [S16][S22][S1]
Risks:
- Gross-margin compression from memory and NAND/DRAM costs: management says these trends will intensify, and the 10-K flags that gross margins are subject to volatility and downward pressure from component costs, pricing and mix [S6][S1]
- Services regulatory risk: DMA fines and periodic penalties in the EU, antitrust suits and a US court order preventing commissions on certain App Store purchases; Services is the 75.4%-margin part of the business [S1][S16][S22]
- Tariff and trade policy: Section 232 semiconductor review, newly imposed Section 301 tariffs and possible retaliation affect supply chain, component availability and gross margin; the tariff refunds that flattered Q3 are non-recurring [S6]
- China demand and competition: Apple's China shipments fell 4.3% in calendar Q3 2026 while the market fell 15.4%, so share gains came from a shrinking pool, and Greater China remains the most iPhone-concentrated region [S18][S1]
- Valuation risk: at 39.4x earnings with a 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield, the multiple has no cushion; a de-rating to the FY2023 28x level alone would cost about 29% [S7][S14]

- Up: gross margin holds at or above 48% into FY2027 after the Q4 step-down, which would validate a 33x base multiple rather than the bear case [S24][S6]
- Up: Services sustains 13%+ growth and China units stabilise, extending the mix shift that carries the 75.4% Services gross margin [S1][S18]
- Down: memory and NAND costs cap gross margin near 45%, cutting EPS by roughly 7% even with revenue growing [S6]
- Down: multiple de-rating from 39.4x toward the 22.0x peer median or the 28x FY2023 level on a higher-for-longer 5.04% Treasury yield [S7][S14]

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## E2 (Market Analyst): Apple Inc. (AAPL): business model, AI position, regulation and competitive position at 29 October 2026
Apple enters late October 2026 with revenue accelerating (nine months to 27 June 2026 up 16%, iPhone up 22%, Services up 14%) on price and mix rather than units, a Chinese rebound that reverses the FY2025 decline, and a gross margin at a record 50.1%. The moat looks intact on switching costs — 2.5bn devices, a 75.4%-margin Services line — but the margin expansion is partly tariff refunds and mix, and the two real threats are the memory oligopoly that set a 350% cost increase and regulation cutting the European take rate. AI capability is now licensed from Google, the single largest strategic concession in the case.
Parts: business, competition
Findings:
- Nine months to 27 June 2026: revenue $364,357m, +16%; iPhone $196,515m, +22%; Services $91,728m, +14%; group gross margin 49.1% versus 46.8% a year earlier [S6].
- Growth is price and mix, not units: Apple's calendar Q3 2026 shipments were 57.3m, down 4.0% in a market down 22%, lifting share to 22.4% from 18.2% [S30], while iPhone revenue rose 22% in the June quarter [S6].
- Greater China reversed: down 4% in FY2025 [S1] to $64,839m and +30% in nine months of FY2026, already above the whole of FY2025, helped by renminbi strength [S6].
- Services were $109,158m in FY2025, 26.2% of revenue at a 75.4% gross margin versus 46.9% group [S1]; on more than 2.5 billion active devices [S28] that is at most $43.7 of Services revenue per device per year (derived).
- AI is outsourced: a non-exclusive multi-year agreement of 12 January 2026 has Apple using Gemini models and Google cloud for future foundation models including Siri [S29], while Apple's own R&D rose 32% to $11,729m in the June quarter on AI infrastructure [S6]; Omdia says AI is not yet a major purchase driver [S30].
- EU exposure is quantified: a EUR 500m DMA fine on 23 April 2025 for anti-steering breaches [S16], and from 1 October 2026 commissions of 26% on in-app purchase, 20% on alternative payment, 15% on link-out and a 5% Core Technology Commission, with acquisition and store services fees eliminated [S32].
- The US DOJ monopolisation case, filed 21 March 2024 with 16 states and the District of Columbia, remains in litigation with relief unquantified on the case page [S34].
- Google's default-search payments of $20bn a year to Apple survived the remedies ruling, but exclusive distribution deals were banned [S31]; Services revenue is not split out in filings, so this concentration cannot be sized from primary sources [S1].
- Cost and tariff picture: memory costs up 350% year on year [S30]; the 10-Q expects NAND/DRAM constraints to intensify, the Section 232 semiconductor review added no tariffs on Apple products on 14 January 2026, the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 20 February 2026 with refunds claimed against product cost of sales, and new Section 301 duties have since been imposed [S6].
- Leadership changed on 1 September 2026 when John Ternus became CEO with Tim Cook as executive chairman [S28]; capital return was $25.8bn of buybacks and $4.0bn of dividends in the June quarter [S6].
- The margin premium is widening on the evidence: group gross margin 44.1% (FY2023), 46.2% (FY2024), 46.9% (FY2025) [S1] and 50.1% in the June 2026 quarter [S6], against Xiaomi at 19.8% overall and 8.5% on handsets [S36], Microsoft's gross-margin percentage falling on AI infrastructure [S33], and Samsung's record KRW89.5tn operating profit earned in memory [S35].
- Market backdrop at 29 October 2026: S&P 500 7,743.98 on 28 October 2026, third straight gain, Fed held at 3.75-4.00% after a September hike that was the first since 2023, AI-linked stocks strained on financing questions [S27]; Apple's market value $5.02tn, up 25.8% in a year [S26].
Risks:
- Memory cost inflation: costs up 350% year on year with Apple's own filing expecting the trend to intensify, which puts the June 2026 50.1% gross margin at risk in FY2027 [S30][S6].
- EU take-rate compression: the DMA fine of EUR 500m and the 1 October 2026 fee schedule cut the highest-margin revenue line, with the risk that the European template spreads to other jurisdictions [S16][S32].
- US antitrust: the DOJ monopolisation case could force changes to the integration between iPhone, wallet, messaging and watch that underpins switching costs [S34].
- Dependence on a competitor for AI: Siri runs on Gemini and Google pays Apple $20bn a year, so capability and cash flow both rest on one rival [S29][S31].
- Demand: the handset market fell 22% in Q3 2026 and replacement cycles are lengthening, so price-led growth may not repeat [S30].
- Execution under new leadership: a hardware engineer became CEO on 1 September 2026 with growth currently coming from price and mix rather than products [S28].
Scenario drivers:
- Up: memory prices normalise in FY2027 while Apple holds 22%+ unit share, converting a cost headwind into product margin recovery [S30][S6].
- Up: Gemini-powered Siri becomes a genuine upgrade driver and lifts the iPhone replacement rate above the current shrinking market [S29][S30].
- Up: Greater China sustains its 30% growth and Services keeps compounding at 14% with no further regulatory action [S6].
- Down: memory inflation persists through FY2027 and product gross margin gives back the June 2026 gains [S30][S6].
- Down: EU remedies extend to link-out pricing and alternative marketplaces across other regions, or a US consent decree forces changes to default and integration rules [S32][S34].
- Down: an appeal cuts or ends the $20bn default-search payments, removing a material but undisclosed share of Services profit [S31].
Counter-evidence: The best-documented case that the premium is not durable: the June 2026 margin expansion came from tariff refunds and product mix, not pricing [S6], so it is not evidence of pricing power; Xiaomi's ASP rose 25.9% at the same time [S36], meaning rivals are also passing through costs, and a normalisation of memory would let Android prices fall back and reverse Apple's mix gain; Omdia states AI is not yet a consumer purchase driver [S30], so the Gemini-powered Siri does not yet create an upgrade cycle; and the highest-margin line, Services at 75.4% [S1], is the line regulation is aimed at, with the EU already fining Apple EUR 500m [S16] and resetting commissions from 1 October 2026 [S32]. On the bear side of the moat argument, unit share gains in a market down 22% [S30] may reflect competitor supply failure rather than durable preference, which is a cyclical, not structural, gain.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Risks and counter-evidence (risks, revision 2 by Lead Analyst, 6,174 characters)
Apple's franchise risk is modest; the priced risk is severe. At 39.4x trailing earnings [S7] the shares have no room for a memory-cost cycle and a European take-rate reset that have both already begun [S30][S32], and that asymmetry — not doubt about the business — is why the name sits on the watchlist rather than in the portfolio.

**Seven risks, ranked by probability and impact**

1. **Memory-cost compression of gross margin — high/high, now into FY2027.** Memory costs are up 350% year on year [S30] and Apple's 10-Q expects NAND/DRAM constraints to intensify [S6]. Q4 FY2026 is guided to 47–48% from the 50.1% just reported, and the guide still contains 1pp of refunds [S17][S24]. Each 100bp of gross margin is $0.26 of EPS, 3.0% of trailing EPS of $8.72 [S6]; the guided 200–300bp step-down is 6–9% of annual EPS [S6][S24]. Manageable, but it is the exact distance between the base and bear cases.

2. **Services take-rate reset — high/high, live from 1 October 2026.** The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 23 April 2025 for breaching the DMA's anti-steering rules [S16]; from 1 October 2026 in-app commission is 26%, alternative payment 20%, link-out 15%, plus a 5% Core Technology Commission [S32]. This attacks the 75.4%-gross-margin line that is 26.2% of revenue [S1], and Apple discloses no Services split, so the damage cannot be sized from filings [S1]. Fatal to the margin premium only if the European template spreads.

3. **Multiple de-rating — medium/high, first test 2 November 2026.** 39.4x against FY2022–FY2025 year-ends of 24.6x–37.5x [S7] and a Microsoft/Alphabet median of 22.0x [S9][S11], with the 10-year Treasury at 5.04% [S14]. A de-rating to 28.0x costs 29%; to 22.0x, 44% [S7][S9][S11]. The largest immediate price consequence in the case sits here, not in the operating business.

4. **China unit erosion under a rebounding revenue line — medium/medium, FY2027.** China shipments fell 15.4% in calendar Q3 2026 and Apple's units fell 4.3%, share rising to 17.8% from 15.8% [S18], while Greater China revenue rose 30% to $64.8bn in nine months on renminbi strength and Pro mix [S6]. The region is 17.8% of revenue [S6]: a share gain inside a shrinking pool is cyclical, not structural.

5. **iPhone concentration and cycle mean reversion — medium/high, FY2027.** iPhone is 53.9% of nine-month revenue [S6] and grew 22% in the June 2026 quarter after 0% in FY2024 and 4% in FY2025 [S1]; the 10-K notes a significant portion of sales comes from a single product category [S1].

6. **Dependence on a competitor — high (structural)/medium.** Siri runs on Gemini under a non-exclusive multi-year agreement of 12 January 2026 [S29], while Google pays $20bn a year to be the default search engine, with exclusivity banned in the remedies ruling [S31]. An appeal that cuts those payments removes a material, undisclosed share of Services profit [S1].

7. **Tariff and trade policy — medium/medium, live.** Section 232 added no tariffs on Apple products on 14 January 2026; the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 20 February 2026 with refunds claimed against product cost of sales; new Section 301 duties have since been imposed [S6]. The refunds that flattered the June quarter do not repeat [S17]. Inventory has already risen to $11.1bn from $5.9bn year on year, a build into shortages that becomes a write-down risk if demand softens [S6].

**The strongest case against the thesis.** The watchlist stance assumes a de-rating that may never come. Apple's 2.7% free-cash-flow yield is the highest in the peer set (Microsoft 1.5%, Alphabet 1.3%) [S7][S9][S11], its 10.6x EV/Sales is below Microsoft's 11.3x despite a structurally higher gross margin [S7][S9][S1], Services compounds at 13% [S1] and buybacks of $82.2bn a year shrink the share count [S6]. A long-only fund that waits for $295–305 [S6][S7] can miss years of that compounding.

**Stress tests.** Revenue 30% lower: on trailing revenue of $466.8bn [S6], holding margins cuts EPS 30% to $6.10, which at 39.4x is $240 [S6][S7] — below the $258 bear case, and it moves the rating from Watchlist to Hold-off until the replacement-cycle trough is visible. Multiple compressed: 28.0x gives −29%, the 22.0x peer median −44% [S7][S9][S11]; with margins intact, $193–244 would clear the $295–305 add trigger and the shares would move to Add, so the watchlist converts the biggest risk into the entry point. Free cash flow 30% lower: $136.7bn becomes $95.7bn [S6], EV/FCF rises to 51.8x and the yield falls to 1.9% [S7]; at the current 2.7% yield the equity would be worth $3.54tn, 29% below the $5.02tn market capitalisation [S6][S7], and the add trigger would fall to $208–215 on 30–31x a 30%-lower earnings base.

| Risk | Probability | Impact | Timing | Signpost | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Financials (financials, revision 3 by Fundamentals Analyst, 5,762 characters)
Apple's profit is compounding faster than revenue, but roughly two of the latest quarter's five points of gross-margin expansion came from one-off tariff refunds [S17] and management has guided the next quarter down to 47–48% [S24]: the earnings quality is thinner than the headline.

**Period.** Apple's fiscal year ends in late September. FY2026 (ended 26 September 2026) was still unreported on 29 October 2026 — the year-end release and call are set for Monday 2 November 2026 [S15]. The last three reported fiscal years are FY2023–FY2025 [S1][S4][S5]; the latest reported quarter is Q3 FY2026, ended 27 June 2026 [S6].

**Segments and mix.** FY2025 revenue rose 6.4% to $416.2bn, with every line except Wearables growing [S1]. Services went from 22.2% of revenue in FY2023 to 26.2% in FY2025 and 28.1% in Q3 FY2026, compounding ~13% a year while the four product lines together grew ~4% [S1][S6]. Q3 FY2026 is a different animal: revenue +16% to $109.4bn and iPhone +22% to $54.3bn [S6][S17], the fastest growth since FY2021. That is an iPhone 17 cycle number, not a new trend line: iPhone grew 0% in FY2024 and 4% in FY2025 on the same base [S1], so +22% will not annualise.

| iPhone | 200,583 | 201,183 | 209,586 | 54,252 (+22%) | [S1][S6] |
| Mac | 29,357 | 29,984 | 33,708 | } 24,426 combined | [S1][S6] |
| iPad | 28,300 | 26,694 | 28,023 | } (derived) | [S1][S6] |
| Wearables, Home & Accessories | 39,845 | 37,005 | 35,686 | } | [S1][S6] |
| Services | 85,200* | 96,169* | 109,158* | 30,739 (+12%) | [S1][S6] |

*Derived: total revenue less the four reported product lines. The Q3 FY2026 excerpt retrieved discloses iPhone and Services individually; the other three categories total $24,426m (derived) [S6].

**Margins.** Group gross margin rose from 44.1% (FY2023) to 46.9% (FY2025) on mix and Services pricing [S1]; Q3 FY2026 hit 50.1%, of which ~2pp was tariff-refund benefit, leaving ~48.1% underlying [S17]. The engine is Services at 75.4% gross margin versus products at ~36.8% (derived: $112.9bn of product gross profit on $307.0bn of product revenue) [S1]. Product margin itself jumped to ~40.1% in Q3 FY2026 from ~34.5% a year earlier (derived), which is mix plus the refund; strip the refund and the durable improvement is far smaller [S6][S17]. Operating margin was 32.0% in FY2025 and 32.6% in Q3 FY2026 despite R&D rising 32.5% year to date to $34.0bn, or 9.3% of revenue versus 8.2% [S1][S6] — Apple's AI spending runs through the income statement, not capex.

**Cash.** Free cash flow is compounding again after stalling: $98.8bn in FY2025, then $136.7bn trailing twelve months to June 2026, +38%, on operating cash flow of $146.7bn [S1][S6]. Conversion is 1.06x net income versus 0.88x in FY2025, so the earnings are cash-backed [S6]. Note where the cash comes from: capex *fell* to $10.0bn trailing from $12.7bn in FY2025 — there is no AI datacentre step-up in Apple's capex line, so FCF is not capex-exposed, though gross margin is exposed to the memory prices AI demand is inflating [S6]. Capital returns have slowed, not accelerated: buybacks of $82.2bn trailing versus $90.7bn in FY2025 and $62.1bn in the first nine months versus $70.6bn [S1][S6], plus $15.6bn of dividends. Net cash rose to $62.2bn from $33.8bn [S6] — management is rebuilding the balance sheet rather than buying stock at today's multiple, which tells you what insiders think of the price.

**Key variable and its sensitivity: component cost.** Apple states that memory (DRAM/NAND) and advanced-semiconductor supply is constrained and that it "expects these trends to intensify" [S6]. Sensitivity: on TTM revenue of $466.8bn, each 100bp of gross margin is $4.67bn pre-tax and about $0.26 of EPS at the 17.3% TTM tax rate, or 3.0% of TTM EPS of $8.72 [S6]. The 200–300bp step-down implied by the Q4 FY2026 guide is therefore worth an estimated 6–9% of annual EPS on the same base [S6][S24]. Demand is the less sensitive variable: revenue growth of 16% would have to halve to matter as much as 200bp of margin.

**Geography and trade.** Greater China fell from $72.6bn (FY2023) to $64.4bn (FY2025) [S1] and then rebounded: +22% to $18.8bn in Q3 FY2026 and +30% to $64.8bn for the nine months, helped by a stronger renminbi and iPhone Pro mix [S6]. That revenue rebound sits against weaker units: IDC puts China smartphone shipments down 15.4% in calendar Q3 2026 with Apple units down 4.3%, though share rose to 17.8% from 15.8% [S18]. On policy, the Section 232 semiconductor review produced no additional tariffs in January 2026 and Apple booked refunds after the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs in February 2026, but new Section 301 tariffs have since been imposed [S6].

**What this means for the investor.** The near-term question is not demand — nine-month revenue rose 16% to $364.4bn and operating income 22% to $122.4bn, with all five regions growing [S6] — but whether the 47–48% gross margin guided for Q4 FY2026 holds into FY2027 [S24]. Held, today's growth rate is worth owning; if memory costs push margin toward 45%, EPS falls by roughly 7% even with revenue still growing [S6]. A single guided step-down after four quarters of expansion is a normal input-cost cycle, not proof of deterioration, and 1.06x cash conversion means the gains so far are being collected rather than accrued [S6].

**Confidence: medium** — the reported figures are filing-grade, but FY2026 is unreported until 2 November 2026, the margin line is unusually policy-dependent (tariff refunds, Section 301), and the China recovery mixes currency and mix with a still-falling unit base [S18].

arguments.markdown:
Apple's franchise risk is modest; the priced risk is severe. At 39.4x trailing earnings [S7] the shares have no room for a memory-cost cycle and a European take-rate reset that have both already begun [S30][S32] — that asymmetry, not doubt about the business, is why the name sits on the watchlist rather than in the portfolio.

**Seven risks, ranked by probability and impact**

1. **Memory-cost compression of gross margin — high/high, into FY2027.** Memory costs are up 350% year on year [S30] and the 10-Q expects NAND/DRAM constraints to intensify [S6]. Q4 FY2026 is guided to 47–48% from the 50.1% just reported [S17][S24]; each 100bp of gross margin is 3.0% of trailing EPS of $8.72, so the guided 200–300bp step-down is 6–9% of annual earnings [S6]. Manageable, but it is the exact distance between the base and bear cases.

2. **Services take-rate reset — high/high, live since 1 October 2026.** The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 23 April 2025 for breaching the DMA's anti-steering rules [S16]; from 1 October 2026 in-app commission is 26%, alternative payment 20%, link-out 15%, plus a 5% Core Technology Commission [S32]. This attacks the 75.4%-gross-margin line that is 26.2% of revenue, and Apple discloses no Services split, so filings cannot size the damage [S1]. Fatal to the margin premium only if the European template spreads.

3. **Multiple de-rating — medium/high, first test 2 November 2026.** 39.4x against FY2022–FY2025 year-ends of 24.6x–37.5x [S7] and a Microsoft/Alphabet median of 22.0x [S9][S11], with the 10-year Treasury at 5.04% [S14]. A de-rating to 28.0x costs 29% and to 22.0x, 44% [S7][S9][S11]. The largest immediate price consequence in the case sits here, not in the operating business.

4. **China unit erosion under a rebounding revenue line — medium/medium, FY2027.** China smartphone shipments fell 15.4% in calendar Q3 2026 and Apple's units 4.3%, with share rising to 17.8% from 15.8% [S18], while Greater China revenue rose 30% to $64.8bn in nine months on renminbi strength and Pro mix [S6]. A share gain inside a shrinking pool is cyclical, not structural.

5. **iPhone cycle mean reversion — medium/high, FY2027.** iPhone is 53.9% of nine-month revenue [S6] and grew 22% in the June 2026 quarter after 0% in FY2024 and 4% in FY2025 [S1]; the 10-K flags reliance on a single product category [S1].

6. **Dependence on a competitor — high (structural)/medium.** Siri runs on Gemini under a non-exclusive multi-year agreement of 12 January 2026 [S29], while Google pays $20bn a year to be the default search engine, with exclusivity banned in the remedies ruling [S31]. An appeal that cuts those payments removes a material, undisclosed share of Services profit [S1].

7. **Tariff and trade policy — medium/medium, live.** Section 232 added no tariffs on Apple products on 14 January 2026; the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 20 February 2026, with refunds claimed against product cost of sales; new Section 301 duties have since been imposed [S6]. The refunds that flattered the June quarter do not repeat [S17].

**The strongest case against the thesis.** The watchlist assumes a de-rating that may never come. Apple's 2.7% free-cash-flow yield is the highest in the peer set (Microsoft 1.5%, Alphabet 1.3%) [S7][S9][S11], its 10.6x EV/Sales is below Microsoft's 11.3x despite a structurally higher gross margin [S7][S9][S1], Services compounds at 13% [S1] and $82.2bn of buybacks a year shrink the share count [S6]. A long-only fund that waits for $305 can miss years of that compounding.

**Stress tests.** Revenue 30% lower cuts EPS 30% to $6.10 on trailing revenue of $466.8bn [S6], which at 39.4x is $240 a share [S7] — below the $258 bear case, and it moves the rating from Watchlist to Hold-off until a replacement-cycle trough is visible. Multiple compressed: 28.0x gives −29% and the 22.0x peer median −44% [S7][S9][S11]; with margins intact that puts the shares at $193–244, through the $305 entry, so the watchlist converts the biggest risk into the entry point and the rating moves to Add. Free cash flow 30% lower takes $136.7bn to $95.7bn [S6], EV/FCF to 51.8x and the yield to 1.9% [S7]; at a 2.7% yield the equity would be worth $3.54tn, 29% below the $5.02tn market capitalisation, and the entry would fall to $208–215.

| Risk | Probability | Impact | Timing | Signpost | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Memory-cost margin reset | High | High | Q4 FY2026–FY2027 | Gross margin below 47% in the 2 November 2026 release | [S24][S30][S6] |
| Services take-rate compression | High | High | Live from 1 Oct 2026 | EU periodic penalties; Services growth below 13% | [S16][S32][S1] |
| Multiple de-rating | Medium | High | Any quarter | 10-year yield above 5.04%; P/E below 33x | [S7][S14] |
| China unit erosion | Medium | Medium | FY2027 | China units falling faster than share rises | [S18] |
| iPhone cycle mean reversion | Medium | High | FY2027 | iPhone growth below 10% in the December 2026 quarter | [S6][S1] |

**What this means for the investor.** None of these risks is fatal alone; three point the same way, into the same quarter. The position stays at zero until the 2 November 2026 print shows whether the margin step-down is an input-cost cycle or a reset [S15].

**Confidence: medium, because** the filing evidence is strong — the memory-cost warning sits in the 10-Q [S6] and the fee schedule in the European Commission's decision record [S16][S32] — but the two largest financial risks, memory prices and EU remedies, sit outside Apple's control and cannot be quantified from its disclosures [S1].

Business text:

**Apple is a $416bn-revenue device franchise [S1] whose fiscal 2026 acceleration comes from iPhone price and mix plus a Chinese rebound rather than unit growth, while its AI capability is rented from Google and its European take rate is being reset by regulation. An owner buys the 2.5bn-device installed base [S28] and its Services annuity while the handset market contracts 20-22% [S30] and memory costs rise 350% [S30].**

**What it sells, to whom, how the money flows**
Apple sells phones, PCs, tablets, wearables and accessories plus advertising, App Store commission, cloud, subscriptions, AppleCare and payments, through five geographic segments to consumers, SMB, education, enterprise and government; 40% of FY2025 net sales were direct and 60% indirect through carriers and resellers [S1].

| Revenue mix, nine months to 27 June 2026 [S6] | $m | YoY | % of total | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone | 196,515 | +22% | 53.9% | [S6] |
| Services | 91,728 | +14% | 25.2% | [S6] |
| Mac, iPad, Wearables (derived) | 76,114 | +4.7% | 20.9% | [S6] |
| Total net sales | 364,357 | +16% | 100% | [S6] |
| Greater China segment | 64,839 | +30% | 17.8% | [S6] |

**Growth is price and mix, not units.** IDC put Apple's calendar Q3 2026 shipments at 57.3m, down 4.0% in a market down 22% [S30], while iPhone revenue rose 22% in the June quarter [S6] — different periods, so read direction, not arithmetic. Services grew 14% [S6], slower than hardware: attach compounds but is not yet the growth engine. FY2025 Services of $109,158m at a 75.4% gross margin [S1] are about $44 per active device a year (derived) [S28].

**Greater China** fell 4% in FY2025 [S1], then rose 30% to $64,839m in nine months, above all of FY2025 [S1][S6], helped by renminbi strength [S6] — a contradiction of the "losing China" thesis at 18% of revenue [S6]. The constraint is Huawei: 21.1% of China's Q3 2026 shipments against Apple's 17.8% on IDC's count, 21.3% against 19.5% on Counterpoint's, with Huawei growing 17-19% as the market fell 10-15% [S38][S39]. Huawei's share of China's $600+ segment is not disclosed in any source retrieved — a named limitation on the premium end of this recovery.

**Moat, evidenced**
Switching costs sit in the installed base plus a software take rate: Services gross margin 75.4% in FY2025 against 46.9% group [S1]; group gross margin 50.1% in the June 2026 quarter from 46.5% a year earlier [S6]. Apple held 22.4% of units in Q3 2026, up from 18.2% [S30], while Xiaomi, OPPO and vivo lost 29-35% of shipments [S30]: under component scarcity, purchasing power is the advantage.

**AI is outsourced.** On 12 January 2026 Apple and Google agreed a non-exclusive multi-year deal to use Gemini models and Google cloud for foundational models including Siri [S29]. R&D rose 32% to $11,729m in the June quarter on AI infrastructure [S6]. The product-level gap narrowed because Google supplies the model; the capability-level gap widened because frontier work sits with Android's owner. Omdia: AI "is not yet a major consumer purchase driver" [S30] — the case rests on price and retention, not an AI cycle.

**Regulation with a bill attached**
- The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 23 April 2025 for breaching the DMA anti-steering obligation [S16].
- EU fees from 1 October 2026: 26% in-app, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-out, 5% Core Technology Commission [S32] — a structural cut Apple does not size.
- The DOJ monopolisation suit, filed 21 March 2024 with 16 states and DC, is still in litigation [S34]; relief is not quantified on the retrieved case page.
- Google search: the court kept $20bn a year of default-search payments but banned exclusivity [S31], a concentration no filing discloses.

**Supply chain.** Memory costs rose 350% year on year [S30]; the 10-Q cites NAND and DRAM constraints and expects the trend "to intensify" [S6]. arguments.markdown:
**Apple is a $416bn-revenue device franchise [S1] whose fiscal 2026 growth comes from iPhone price and mix plus a Chinese rebound, not units, while its AI is rented from Google and its European take rate is being reset by regulation. An owner buys the 2.5bn-device installed base [S28] and its Services annuity as the handset market contracts 20-22% [S30] and memory costs rise 350% [S30].**

**What it sells, to whom, how the money flows**
Apple sells phones, PCs, tablets, wearables and accessories plus advertising, App Store commission, cloud, subscriptions, AppleCare and payments, through five geographic segments to consumers, SMB, education, enterprise and government; 40% of FY2025 net sales were direct and 60% indirect through carriers and resellers [S1].

| Revenue mix, nine months to 27 June 2026 [S6] | $m | YoY | % of total | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone | 196,515 | +22% | 53.9% | [S6] |
| Services | 91,728 | +14% | 25.2% | [S6] |
| Mac, iPad, Wearables (derived) | 76,114 | +4.7% | 20.9% | [S6] |
| Total net sales | 364,357 | +16% | 100% | [S6] |
| Greater China segment | 64,839 | +30% | 17.8% | [S6] |

**Growth is price and mix, not units.** IDC put Apple's calendar Q3 2026 shipments at 57.3m, down 4.0% in a market down 22% [S30], while iPhone revenue rose 22% in the June quarter [S6] — different periods, so read direction, not arithmetic. Services grew 14% [S6], slower than hardware: attach compounds but is not yet the growth engine. FY2025 Services of $109,158m at a 75.4% gross margin [S1] are about $44 per active device a year (derived) [S28].

**Greater China** fell 4% in FY2025 [S1], then rose 30% to $64,839m in nine months, above all of FY2025 [S1][S6], helped by renminbi strength [S6] — a contradiction of the "losing China" thesis at 18% of revenue [S6]. The constraint is Huawei: 21.1% of China's Q3 2026 shipments against Apple's 17.8% on IDC's count, 21.3% against 19.5% on Counterpoint's, with Huawei growing 17-19% as the market fell 10-15% [S38][S39]. Huawei's share of China's $600+ segment is not disclosed in any source retrieved — a named limitation on the premium end of this recovery.

**Moat, evidenced**
Switching costs sit in the installed base plus a software take rate: Services gross margin 75.4% [S1], group gross margin 50.1% in the June 2026 quarter from 46.5% a year earlier [S6]. Apple held 22.4% of units in Q3 2026, up from 18.2% [S30], while Xiaomi, OPPO and vivo lost 29-35% of shipments [S30]: under component scarcity, purchasing power wins.

**AI is outsourced.** On 12 January 2026 Apple and Google agreed a non-exclusive multi-year deal to use Gemini models and Google cloud for foundational models including Siri [S29]. R&D rose 32% to $11,729m in the June quarter on AI infrastructure [S6]. The product-level gap narrowed because Google supplies the model; the capability-level gap widened because frontier work sits with Android's owner. Omdia: AI "is not yet a major consumer purchase driver" [S30] — the case rests on price and retention, not an AI cycle.

**Regulation with a bill attached**
- The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 23 April 2025 for breaching the DMA anti-steering obligation [S16].
- EU fees from 1 October 2026: 26% in-app, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-out, 5% Core Technology Commission [S32] — a structural cut Apple does not size.
- The DOJ monopolisation suit, filed 21 March 2024 with 16 states and DC, is still in litigation [S34]; relief is not quantified on the retrieved case page.
- Google search: the court kept $20bn a year of default-search payments but banned exclusivity [S31], a concentration no filing discloses.

**Supply chain.** Memory costs rose 350% year on year [S30]; the 10-Q cites NAND and DRAM constraints and expects the trend "to intensify" [S6]. The Section 232 semiconductor review imposed no new tariffs on Apple products on 14 January 2026; the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 20 February 2026 and Apple claimed refunds, while new Section 301 duties followed [S6]. Apple does not disclose country-level assembly, so the India ramp cannot be sized.

**Management and milestones.** Ternus became CEO on 1 September 2026 with Cook as executive chairman [S28] — a hardware engineer inheriting price-led growth, the judgement to test; buybacks were $25.8bn and dividends $4.0bn in the June quarter [S6].
- 12 Jan 2026: Gemini agreement [S29]
- 20 Apr 2026: Ternus named CEO, effective 1 Sep [S28]
- 31 Jul 2026: Q3 FY2026 filed, revenue +16%, margin 50.1% [S6]
- 1 Oct 2026: EU fee schedule effective [S32]
- Q3 2026: unit share 22.4%, up 4.2pp year on year [S30]

**Backdrop at 29 October 2026.** The S&P 500 closed at 7,743.98 on 28 October 2026 and the Nasdaq at 26,549.85 [S27]; the Fed held at 3.75-4.00% after a September hike [S27]. Apple's market value was $5.02tn, up 25.8% in a year [S26].

**Confidence: high, because mix, margin and regulatory facts come from Apple's filings and the European Commission, with two research houses corroborating share; the unresolved items are Services concentration, the unmeasured China premium split and the durability of a memory-driven margin.**

2. **Services take-rate reset — high/high, live since 1 October 2026.** The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 23 April 2025 [S16]; in-app commission is now 26%, alternative payment 20%, link-out 15%, plus a 5% Core Technology Commission [S32]. 3. **Multiple de-rating — medium/high, first test 2 November 2026.** 39.4x against FY2022–FY2025 year-ends of 24.6–37.5x [S7] and a Microsoft/Alphabet median of 22.0x [S9][S11], with the 10-year at 5.04% [S14]: 28.0x costs 29%, 22.0x costs 44% [S7].

5. **iPhone cycle mean reversion — medium/high, FY2027.** iPhone is 53.9% of nine-month revenue [S6] and grew 22% in the June 2026 quarter after 0% in FY2024 and 4% in FY2025 [S1].

6. **Dependence on a competitor — high (structural)/medium.** Siri runs on Gemini under a non-exclusive agreement of 12 January 2026 [S29], while Google pays $20bn a year to be the default search engine, with exclusivity banned in the remedies ruling [S31]; an appeal that cuts those payments would remove a material, undisclosed share of Services profit [S1].

7. **Trade policy — medium/medium, live.** Section 232 added no tariffs on Apple products on 14 January 2026 and the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 20 February 2026, but new Section 301 duties have since been imposed, and the refunds that flattered the June quarter do not repeat [S6][S17].

**The strongest case against the thesis.** The watchlist assumes a de-rating that may never come. Apple's 2.7% free-cash-flow yield is the highest in the peer set (Microsoft 1.5%, Alphabet 1.3%) [S7][S9][S11], its 10.6x EV/Sales is below Microsoft's 11.3x despite a higher gross margin [S7][S9][S1], Services compounds at 13% [S1] and buybacks shrink the count [S6]. Free cash flow 30% lower takes $136.7bn to $95.7bn [S6], EV/FCF to 51.8x and the yield to 1.9% [S7]; at a 2.7% yield the equity is worth $3.54tn, 29% below the $5.02tn market capitalisation.

arguments.markdown:
Apple's franchise risk is modest; the priced risk is severe. At 39.4x trailing earnings [S7] the shares have no room for a memory-cost cycle and a European take-rate reset that have both begun [S30][S32].

**Seven risks, ranked by probability and impact**

1. **Memory-cost margin reset — high/high, into FY2027.** Memory costs are up 350% year on year [S30] and the 10-Q expects NAND/DRAM constraints to intensify [S6]. Q4 FY2026 is guided to 47–48% from 50.1% [S17][S24], and each 100bp is 3.0% of trailing EPS, so the guide is 6–9% of annual earnings [S6].

2. **Services take-rate reset — high/high, live since 1 October 2026.** The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 23 April 2025 [S16]; commissions are now 26% in-app, 20% on alternative payment, 15% on link-out, plus a 5% Core Technology Commission [S32]. That taxes the 75.4%-margin line that is 26.2% of revenue, and no Services split lets filings size it [S1].

3. **Multiple de-rating — medium/high, first test 2 November 2026.** 39.4x against FY2022–FY2025 year-ends of 24.6–37.5x [S7] and a Microsoft/Alphabet median of 22.0x [S9][S11], with the 10-year at 5.04% [S14]: 28.0x costs 29% and 22.0x costs 44% [S7].

4. **China unit erosion under a rebounding revenue line — medium/medium, FY2027.** China shipments fell 15.4% in calendar Q3 2026 and Apple's units 4.3%, with share rising to 17.8% from 15.8% [S18], while Greater China revenue rose 30% to $64.8bn in nine months on renminbi strength and Pro mix [S6].

5. **iPhone cycle mean reversion — medium/high, FY2027.** iPhone is 53.9% of nine-month revenue [S6] and grew 22% in the June 2026 quarter after 0% in FY2024 and 4% in FY2025 [S1].

6. **Dependence on a competitor — high/medium.** Siri runs on Gemini under a non-exclusive agreement of 12 January 2026 [S29], while Google pays $20bn a year to be the default search engine with exclusivity banned [S31]; a cut to those payments would remove a material, undisclosed share of Services profit [S1].

7. **Trade policy — medium/medium, live.** Section 232 added no tariffs on Apple products in January 2026 and the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs in February, but new Section 301 duties have since been imposed and the refunds that flattered the June quarter do not repeat [S6][S17].

**The strongest case against the thesis.** The watchlist assumes a de-rating that may never come. Apple's 2.7% free-cash-flow yield is the highest of the peer set (Microsoft 1.5%, Alphabet 1.3%) [S7][S9][S11], its 10.6x EV/Sales is below Microsoft's 11.3x despite a higher gross margin [S7][S9][S1], Services compounds at 13% [S1] and buybacks shrink the count [S6]. A fund that waits for the entry price can miss years of that compounding.

**Stress tests.** Revenue 30% lower cuts EPS 30% to $6.10 on $466.8bn of trailing revenue [S6], which at 39.4x is $240 [S7] — below the $258 bear case, moving the rating to Hold-off until a replacement-cycle trough is visible. Multiple compressed: 28.0x gives −29% and 22.0x −44% [S7][S9][S11]; with margins intact that is $193–244, through the $305 entry, so the watchlist converts the biggest risk into the entry point and the rating to Add. Free cash flow 30% lower takes $136.7bn to $95.7bn [S6], EV/FCF to 51.8x and the yield to 1.9% [S7]; at a 2.7% yield the equity is worth $3.54tn, 29% below the $5.02tn market capitalisation.

| Services take-rate reset | High | High | Live from 1 Oct 2026 | EU periodic penalties; Services below 13% | [S16][S32][S1] |
| Multiple de-rating | Medium | High | Any quarter | 10-year above 5.04%; P/E below 33x | [S7][S14] |

| Trade policy | Medium | Medium | Live | New Section 301 duties; refunds end | [S6][S17] |

**What this means for the investor.** No risk here is fatal alone, but three point the same way, into the same quarter. The position stays at zero until the 2 November 2026 print shows whether the margin step-down is an input-cost cycle or a reset [S15].

**Confidence: medium, because** the filing evidence is strong — the memory warning sits in the 10-Q [S6], the fee schedule in the European Commission's record [S16][S32] — but the two largest risks, memory prices and EU remedies, sit outside Apple's control and cannot be quantified from its disclosures [S1].

The scenario work argues for a watchlist, not a position: the probability-weighted value of $330.50 is 3.9% below today's $343.83 and all three cases land within 25% of the price [S6][S7][S24]. The distribution is skewed the wrong way for a buyer and the right way for a patient one, because the largest driver — FY2027 gross margin — is tested on 2 November 2026 [S15].

**Bull — 25%, $410, +19%.** Memory prices normalise, Apple holds 22%+ unit share [S30], gross margin reaches 48.5% and Services compounds at 13% on a 75.4% margin [S1]. Revenue grows 11%, EPS reaches $10.80 and the multiple stays at 38.0x, the highest Apple has sustained [S7]. Signposts: gross margin at or above 48% on 2 November [S15][S24]; NAND/DRAM spot prices falling [S30]; Gemini-powered Siri driving replacements [S29].

**Base — 50%, $327, −5%.** Revenue grows 7%, gross margin settles at 47.5% in line with the Q4 guide [S24], EPS is $9.90 and the multiple holds 33.0x [S9][S11]. That 33.0x is a deliberate premium to the 22.0x Microsoft/Alphabet median and 16% below today's 39.4x: it sits below Apple's FY2024 (37.5x) and FY2025 (34.2x) year-ends and above its 31.1x four-year median [S7], and it pays for a 2.7% free-cash-flow yield against Microsoft's 1.5% and Alphabet's 1.3% [S7][S9][S11]. If that premium closes, the same $9.90 is worth $274 at Microsoft's 27.7x and $218 at 22.0x — 20% and 37% below today.

**Bear — 25%, $258, −25%.** Revenue grows 2%, memory costs hold gross margin at 45.5% [S30][S6], EU remedies trim the Services take rate [S32] and the multiple de-rates to 28.0x, the FY2023 year-end level [S7], on EPS of $9.20. Signposts: a Q4 miss against the 47–48% guide [S24]; EU periodic penalties [S16]; China units falling faster than share rises [S18].

**The assumptions that matter, and the bridge to each EPS.** FY2026E EPS of $8.87 is nine-month actuals of $6.88 plus a $1.99 fourth-quarter estimate [S6][S25]. From there each point of revenue growth is worth about 1.0% of EPS, each 100bp of gross margin $0.26 or 3.0% of EPS, and buybacks at $82.2bn a year about 1.6% of the share count [S6][S7]. Base reconciles as 7pp of growth, 1.6pp from buybacks and 3.0pp of Services mix and opex leverage; the bull needs 6.2pp and the bear 6.1pp from that same mix line, which is the judgement in the band and the most likely place for it to be wrong.

| Services mix and opex (residual) | +6.1pp | +3.0pp | +6.2pp | Implied; Services +13% vs products ~4% | [S1] |
| Exit multiple | 28.0x | 33.0x | 38.0x | 5x on $9.90 of EPS is $49.50 a share | [S7] |

| Bull | 25% | Memory normalises, 48.5% margin, 11% growth, 38.0x | $410, +19% | Margin ≥48% on 2 Nov 2026; memory spot falling | [S1][S7][S24][S30] |

**What the range says about the price.** Even the bull case returns 19% over the 12–18 month horizon against a 5.04% ten-year Treasury [S14] and a 2.7% free-cash-flow yield [S7]: the upside is a multiple that stays at its historical peak, not one that expands. The base case pays nothing for waiting and the bear takes a quarter of the capital, which at 39.4x trailing earnings [S7] is the wrong shape for a long-only book.

**Position sizing: watchlist, zero now.** The add trigger: enter at or below $305 a share — 30.8x FY2027E EPS of $9.90 and 11% below the 28 October 2026 close; a starter position of half a normal weight on entry; full weight only once FY2027 gross margin of 47.5% or better is confirmed in guidance or filings, first test the 2 November 2026 results [S15][S24]. If the price never comes, the compounding case in the risks part is the reason to revisit the trigger rather than the rating.

**Confidence: medium, because** the band rests on filing-grade FY2025 and nine-month FY2026 figures [S1][S6] and a timestamped price [S7], but every FY2027 input is an estimate until Apple reports on 2 November 2026 [S15], and the probabilities are our judgement rather than a market-implied distribution.

**Apple is a $416bn-revenue device franchise [S1] whose fiscal 2026 growth comes from iPhone price and mix plus a Chinese rebound, not units, while its AI is rented from Google and its European take rate is being reset by regulation. An owner buys the 2.5bn-device installed base [S28] and its Services annuity into a contracting handset market [S30].**

**What it sells, to whom, how the money flows**
Apple sells phones, PCs, tablets, wearables and accessories plus advertising, App Store commission, cloud, subscriptions, AppleCare and payments, through five geographic segments to consumers, SMB, education, enterprise and government; 40% of FY2025 net sales were direct and 60% indirect through carriers and resellers [S1].

| Revenue mix, nine months to 27 June 2026 [S6] | $m | YoY | % of total | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone | 196,515 | +22% | 53.9% | [S6] |
| Services | 91,728 | +14% | 25.2% | [S6] |
| Mac, iPad, Wearables | 76,114 | +4.7% | 20.9% | [S6] |
| Total net sales | 364,357 | +16% | 100% | [S6] |
| Greater China segment | 64,839 | +30% | 17.8% | [S6] |

**Growth is price and mix, not units.** IDC put Apple's calendar Q3 2026 shipments at 57.3m, down 4.0% in a market down 22% [S30], while iPhone revenue rose 22% in the June quarter [S6] — different periods, so read direction. Services grew 14% [S6], slower than hardware: attach compounds but is not yet the growth engine. FY2025 Services of $109,158m at a 75.4% gross margin [S1] are about $44 per active device a year (derived) [S28].

**Greater China** fell 4% in FY2025 [S1], then rose 30% to $64,839m in nine months, above all of FY2025 [S1][S6], helped by renminbi strength [S6] — a contradiction of the "losing China" thesis at 18% of revenue [S6]. The constraint is Huawei: 21.1% of China's Q3 2026 shipments against Apple's 17.8% on IDC's count, 21.3% against 19.5% on Counterpoint's, with Huawei growing 17-19% as the market fell 10-15% [S38][S39]. No retrieved source sizes Huawei's share of China's premium segment — a named limitation on this recovery.

**Moat, evidenced**
Switching costs sit in the installed base plus a software take rate: Services gross margin 75.4% [S1], group gross margin 50.1% in the June 2026 quarter from 46.5% a year earlier [S6]. Apple held 22.4% of units in Q3 2026, up from 18.2% [S30], while Xiaomi, OPPO and vivo lost 29-35% of shipments [S30]: under component scarcity, purchasing power wins.

**AI is outsourced.** On 12 January 2026 Apple and Google agreed a non-exclusive multi-year deal to use Gemini models and Google cloud for foundational models including Siri [S29]. R&D rose 32% to $11,729m in the June quarter on AI infrastructure [S6]. The product-level gap narrowed because Google supplies the model; the capability-level gap widened because frontier work sits with Android's owner. Omdia: AI "is not yet a major consumer purchase driver" [S30] — the case rests on price and retention, not an AI cycle.

**Regulation with a bill attached**
- The Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 23 April 2025 for breaching the DMA anti-steering rule [S16].
- EU fees from 1 October 2026: 26% in-app, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-out, 5% Core Technology Commission [S32] — a structural cut Apple does not size.
- The DOJ monopolisation suit, filed 21 March 2024 with 16 states and DC, is still in litigation [S34]; relief is not quantified on the retrieved case page.
- Google search: the court kept $20bn a year of default-search payments but banned exclusivity [S31] — a concentration no filing discloses.

**Supply chain.** Memory costs rose 350% year on year [S30]; the 10-Q cites NAND and DRAM constraints and expects the trend "to intensify" [S6]. Section 232 imposed no new semiconductor tariffs on Apple on 14 January 2026; the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 20 February 2026 and Apple claimed refunds, while new Section 301 duties followed [S6]. Apple does not disclose country-level assembly, so the India ramp cannot be sized.

**Management and milestones.** Ternus became CEO on 1 September 2026 with Cook as executive chairman [S28] — a hardware engineer inheriting price-led growth, the judgement to test; buybacks were $25.8bn and dividends $4.0bn in the June quarter [S6].

- 20 Apr 2026: Ternus named CEO, effective 1 Sep [S28]

- 1 Oct 2026: EU fee schedule effective [S32]
- Q3 2026: unit share 22.4%, up 4.2pp year on year [S30]

**Backdrop at 29 October 2026.** S&P 500 7,743.98 and Nasdaq 26,549.85 at the 28 October close [S27]; the Fed held at 3.75-4.00% after a September hike [S27]. Apple was worth $5.02tn, up 25.8% in a year [S26].

arguments.summary: Revised business (4,993 chars) and competition (4,943 chars), both passing. Added a dollar-sized market estimate independent of the IDC/Omdia unit article (TechInsights: $107.5bn Q1 2026 wholesale revenue, Apple $57.0bn and a record 53% of value), Apple's share by value, and Huawei's China share from two research houses (IDC 21.1%, Counterpoint 21.3% in Q3 2026). Huawei's share of China's premium ($600+) segment could not be retrieved and is stated as a named limitation in both parts. Business was cut from 5,552 to 4,993 characters by removing restated figures, not evidence.
findings: Global smartphone wholesale revenue was $107.5bn in Q1 2026, up 12% YoY while shipments fell 2.2%; Apple's revenue rose 22% to $57.0bn for a record 53% value share, and the $1,000+ tier reached $38.2bn, 35.5% of revenue [S37].
Apple shipped 57.3m phones in Q3 2026, -4.0%, for 22.4% of a market that fell 22% to 255.3m units, against Samsung's 57.8m and 22.6% (-5.8%) and Xiaomi's 30.7m and 12.0% (-29.2%) [S30].
Huawei led China's Q3 2026 smartphone market with 21.1% share on IDC's preliminary count (12.2m units, +17.3%) while Apple held 17.8% (-4.3%) in a market down 15.4% to 57.9m units [S38].

Counterpoint's method gives Huawei 21.3% and Apple 19.5% of China in Q3 2026 (Apple up from 14.7%), the two combined at 40.8% versus 30.7% a year earlier, with Huawei shipments +19% as the market fell 10% [S39].
Omdia separately puts China's Q3 2026 shipments at 59.3m units (-12%), with Huawei 12.4m and Apple 11.6m, a third method pointing the same way on vendor order [S39].
Greater China revenue was $64,839m in the nine months to 27 June 2026, +30% and above all of FY2025, after a 4% decline in FY2025, helped by renminbi strength [S1][S6].
Group gross margin was 50.1% in the June 2026 quarter, including about 2pp from tariff refunds, against 46.5% a year earlier; the 10-Q expects memory cost pressure to intensify [S6].

The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 23 April 2025 for the DMA anti-steering breach; EU commissions were cut from 1 October 2026 to 26% in-app, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-out and 5% Core Technology Commission [S16][S32].

Apple's AI position is rented: a non-exclusive multi-year Gemini and Google Cloud agreement signed 12 January 2026 covers foundational models including Siri, while Omdia calls AI not yet a major purchase driver [S29][S30].
Huawei's share of China's $600+ premium segment in Q3 2026 was not retrieved: Counterpoint and Omdia pages returned HTTP 403, so the premium end of Apple's China recovery is unmeasured [S38][S39].
risks: Memory cost inflation of 350% YoY is set by Samsung and other suppliers, not Apple, and the 10-Q expects it to intensify: FY2027 gross margin, not revenue, is exposed [S6][S30][S35].
EU DMA enforcement: a EUR 500m fine already paid and a commission schedule cut from 1 October 2026 that reduces App Store economics Apple does not size [S16][S32].
US DOJ monopolisation case filed 21 March 2024 with 16 states and DC remains in litigation with unquantified relief [S34].
Huawei leads China overall (21.1-21.3% versus Apple's 17.8-19.5%) and its premium-segment share is unmeasured, so a mix-led China recovery could reverse without showing in unit share [S38][S39].

Alphabet is simultaneously model supplier for Siri, $20bn-a-year search paymaster and Android rival; exclusivity was banned, so the search payment stream is less certain than the amount suggests [S29][S31].

Tariff regime churn: IEEPA tariffs struck down 20 February 2026 with refunds claimed, while new Section 301 duties followed, moving landed cost with no country-level assembly disclosure to size it [S6].
scenario_drivers: Memory price normalisation would let Android rivals cut prices; Apple's unit-share gain and mix benefit reverse together [S30][S36].
Publication of Huawei's China $600+ share would settle whether Apple's China growth is premium share gain or a mid-market rebound [S38][S39].
Further DMA action or DOJ remedies that reach the Services take rate would attack the 75.4% gross-margin line directly [S1][S16][S32][S34].
A quantified Gemini commercial term or an Apple-owned model would change the AI read from rented to owned capability [S29][S6].
Services growth excluding App Store commission, which Apple does not disclose, is the cleanest test of whether regulation is biting [S1][S6].
arguments.counter_evidence: Part of Apple's 50.1% gross margin is bought, not earned: about 2pp came from tariff refunds plus favourable mix in the June 2026 quarter [S6], while 350% memory inflation is a cost Apple cannot control and Samsung earns record operating profit from the same scarcity [S30][S35]. Huawei now leads China's market on both IDC and Counterpoint counts and grew 17-19% while the market fell [S38][S39], and the premium split that would show whether it is winning at Apple's price point is unavailable. AI is not yet a purchase driver [S30], and EU commission cuts plus the EUR 500m fine attack the 75.4%-margin Services line [S16][S32].
gaps: Huawei's share of China's $600+ premium segment in Q3 2026 is not in any retrievable source; Counterpoint and Omdia article pages returned HTTP 403 and the search allowance was exhausted. Stated as a named limitation in both parts.
The dollar-sized market estimate is Q1 2026 (TechInsights), not Q3 2026; no Q3 2026 global revenue figure in dollars was retrieved. Stated in the competition part.
Apple discloses no Services revenue split by category, so DMA damage and Google search concentration cannot be sized.
Samsung's handset-only profitability and Apple's country-level assembly/India share are not disclosed in retrievable sources.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Risks and counter-evidence (risks, revision 4 by Lead Analyst, 4,754 characters)
Apple's franchise risk is modest; the priced risk is severe. At 39.4x trailing earnings [S7] the shares have no room for a memory-cost cycle and a European take-rate reset that have both begun [S30][S32].

**Seven risks, ranked by probability and impact**

1. **Memory-cost margin reset — high/high, into FY2027.** Memory costs are up 350% year on year [S30] and the 10-Q expects NAND/DRAM constraints to intensify [S6]. Q4 FY2026 is guided to 47–48% from 50.1% [S17][S24], and each 100bp is 3.0% of trailing EPS, so the guide is 6–9% of annual earnings [S6].

2. **Services take-rate reset — high/high, live since 1 October 2026.** The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 23 April 2025 [S16]; commissions are now 26% in-app, 20% on alternative payment, 15% on link-out, plus a 5% Core Technology Commission [S32]. That taxes the 75.4%-margin line that is 26.2% of revenue, and no Services split lets filings size it [S1].

3. **Multiple de-rating — medium/high, first test 2 November 2026.** 39.4x against FY2022–FY2025 year-ends of 24.6–37.5x [S7] and a Microsoft/Alphabet median of 22.0x [S9][S11], with the 10-year at 5.04% [S14]: 28.0x costs 29% and 22.0x costs 44% [S7].

4. **China unit erosion under a rebounding revenue line — medium/medium, FY2027.** China shipments fell 15.4% in calendar Q3 2026 and Apple's units 4.3%, with share rising to 17.8% from 15.8% [S18], while Greater China revenue rose 30% to $64.8bn in nine months on renminbi strength and Pro mix [S6].

5. **iPhone cycle mean reversion — medium/high, FY2027.** iPhone is 53.9% of nine-month revenue [S6] and grew 22% in the June 2026 quarter after 0% in FY2024 and 4% in FY2025 [S1].

6. **Dependence on a competitor — high/medium.** Siri runs on Gemini under a non-exclusive agreement of 12 January 2026 [S29], while Google pays $20bn a year to be the default search engine with exclusivity banned [S31]; a cut to those payments would remove a material, undisclosed share of Services profit [S1].

7. **Trade policy — medium/medium, live.** Section 232 added no tariffs on Apple products in January 2026 and the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs in February, but new Section 301 duties have since been imposed and the refunds that flattered the June quarter do not repeat [S6][S17].

**The strongest case against the thesis.** The watchlist assumes a de-rating that may never come. Apple's 2.7% free-cash-flow yield is the highest of the peer set (Microsoft 1.5%, Alphabet 1.3%) [S7][S9][S11], its 10.6x EV/Sales is below Microsoft's 11.3x despite a higher gross margin [S7][S9][S1], Services compounds at 13% [S1] and buybacks shrink the count [S6]. A fund that waits for the entry price can miss years of that compounding.

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## Business (business, revision 6 by Market Analyst, 4,993 characters)
**Apple is a $416bn-revenue device franchise [S1] whose fiscal 2026 growth comes from iPhone price and mix plus a Chinese rebound, not units, while its AI is rented from Google and its European take rate is being reset by regulation. An owner buys the 2.5bn-device installed base [S28] and its Services annuity into a contracting handset market [S30].**

**What it sells, to whom, how the money flows**
Apple sells phones, PCs, tablets, wearables and accessories plus advertising, App Store commission, cloud, subscriptions, AppleCare and payments, through five geographic segments to consumers, SMB, education, enterprise and government; 40% of FY2025 net sales were direct and 60% indirect through carriers and resellers [S1].

| Revenue mix, nine months to 27 June 2026 [S6] | $m | YoY | % of total | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPhone | 196,515 | +22% | 53.9% | [S6] |
| Services | 91,728 | +14% | 25.2% | [S6] |
| Mac, iPad, Wearables | 76,114 | +4.7% | 20.9% | [S6] |
| Total net sales | 364,357 | +16% | 100% | [S6] |
| Greater China segment | 64,839 | +30% | 17.8% | [S6] |

**Growth is price and mix, not units.** IDC put Apple's calendar Q3 2026 shipments at 57.3m, down 4.0% in a market down 22% [S30], while iPhone revenue rose 22% in the June quarter [S6] — different periods, so read direction. Services grew 14% [S6], slower than hardware: attach compounds but is not yet the growth engine. FY2025 Services of $109,158m at a 75.4% gross margin [S1] are about $44 per active device a year (derived) [S28].

**Greater China** fell 4% in FY2025 [S1], then rose 30% to $64,839m in nine months, above all of FY2025 [S1][S6], helped by renminbi strength [S6] — a contradiction of the "losing China" thesis at 18% of revenue [S6]. The constraint is Huawei: 21.1% of China's Q3 2026 shipments against Apple's 17.8% on IDC's count, 21.3% against 19.5% on Counterpoint's, with Huawei growing 17-19% as the market fell 10-15% [S38][S39]. No retrieved source sizes Huawei's share of China's premium segment — a named limitation on this recovery.

**Moat, evidenced**
Switching costs sit in the installed base plus a software take rate: Services gross margin 75.4% [S1], group gross margin 50.1% in the June 2026 quarter from 46.5% a year earlier [S6]. Apple held 22.4% of units in Q3 2026, up from 18.2% [S30], while Xiaomi, OPPO and vivo lost 29-35% of shipments [S30]: under component scarcity, purchasing power wins.

**AI is outsourced.** On 12 January 2026 Apple and Google agreed a non-exclusive multi-year deal to use Gemini models and Google cloud for foundational models including Siri [S29]. R&D rose 32% to $11,729m in the June quarter on AI infrastructure [S6]. The product-level gap narrowed because Google supplies the model; the capability-level gap widened because frontier work sits with Android's owner. Omdia: AI "is not yet a major consumer purchase driver" [S30] — the case rests on price and retention, not an AI cycle.

**Regulation with a bill attached**
- The Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 23 April 2025 for breaching the DMA anti-steering rule [S16].
- EU fees from 1 October 2026: 26% in-app, 20% alternative payment, 15% link-out, 5% Core Technology Commission [S32] — a structural cut Apple does not size.
- The DOJ monopolisation suit, filed 21 March 2024 with 16 states and DC, is still in litigation [S34]; relief is not quantified on the retrieved case page.
- Google search: the court kept $20bn a year of default-search payments but banned exclusivity [S31] — a concentration no filing discloses.

**Supply chain.** Memory costs rose 350% year on year [S30]; the 10-Q cites NAND and DRAM constraints and expects the trend "to intensify" [S6]. Section 232 imposed no new semiconductor tariffs on Apple on 14 January 2026; the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs on 20 February 2026 and Apple claimed refunds, while new Section 301 duties followed [S6]. Apple does not disclose country-level assembly, so the India ramp cannot be sized.

**Management and milestones.** Ternus became CEO on 1 September 2026 with Cook as executive chairman [S28] — a hardware engineer inheriting price-led growth, the judgement to test; buybacks were $25.8bn and dividends $4.0bn in the June quarter [S6].
- 12 Jan 2026: Gemini agreement [S29]
- 20 Apr 2026: Ternus named CEO, effective 1 Sep [S28]
- 31 Jul 2026: Q3 FY2026 filed, revenue +16%, margin 50.1% [S6]
- 1 Oct 2026: EU fee schedule effective [S32]
- Q3 2026: unit share 22.4%, up 4.2pp year on year [S30]

**Backdrop at 29 October 2026.** S&P 500 7,743.98 and Nasdaq 26,549.85 at the 28 October close [S27]; the Fed held at 3.75-4.00% after a September hike [S27]. Apple was worth $5.02tn, up 25.8% in a year [S26].

**Confidence: high, because mix, margin and regulatory facts come from Apple's filings and the European Commission, with two research houses corroborating share; the open items are Services concentration, the unmeasured China premium split and the durability of the margin.**

## Competition and market (competition, revision 5 by Market Analyst, 4,943 characters)
**Apple's gross-margin premium is widening, not narrowing: 50.1% in the June 2026 quarter [S6] against Xiaomi's 19.8% [S36]. The threat is not a better phone but a memory oligopoly setting Apple's bill of materials, Huawei taking China's premium end, and regulators resetting the take rate.**

**Market size: units fall, dollars hold**
| Global smartphone market | Value | YoY | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shipments, Q3 2026 (IDC) | 255.3m units | -22% | [S30] |
| Wholesale revenue, Q1 2026 (TechInsights) | $107.5bn | +12% | [S37] |
| Apple revenue, Q1 2026 (TechInsights) | $57.0bn, 53% of value | +22% | [S37] |
| Samsung, Q3 2026 | 57.8m units, 22.6% | -5.8% | [S30] |
| Apple, Q3 2026 | 57.3m units, 22.4% | -4.0% | [S30] |
| Xiaomi, Q3 2026 | 30.7m units, 12.0% | -29.2% | [S30] |
| Huawei, China Q3 2026 | 12.2m units, 21.1% | +17.3% | [S38] |

IDC and Omdia differ by 2pp on the Q3 decline (22% vs 20%) but both call it the worst in over a decade, caused by supply: memory costs up 350% [S30]. The independent dollar measure is TechInsights: $107.5bn of wholesale revenue in Q1 2026, Apple $57.0bn and a record 53% of value [S37] — about half the industry's revenue on a fifth of its units. Limitation: the dollar split is Q1 2026, not Q3, and no retrieved source gives Huawei's share of China's premium segment in Q3 2026, so whether it gains at Apple's price point or below it cannot be measured.

Services is sized only by Apple: $109,158m in FY2025, up 13.5% at a 75.4% gross margin [S1]; $91,728m in nine months of FY2026, up 14% [S6].

| Competitor comparison | Latest reported evidence | Read | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apple | Q3 FY2026 revenue +16%, gross margin 50.1%, 22.4% unit share | Taking share while units fall | [S6][S30] |
| Samsung Electronics | Q2 2026 revenue KRW171.5tn, operating profit KRW89.5tn, record | Profit earned in memory, not handsets | [S35] |
| Xiaomi | Q2 2026 revenue RMB108.9bn, phone gross margin 8.5%, ASP +25.9%, units -26.5% | Cannot hold share without price | [S36] |
| Microsoft | FY2026 Q3 revenue $82.9bn, +18%, gross margin percentage down | AI capex compresses margins | [S33] |
| Alphabet | Supplies Gemini for Siri; pays Apple $20bn a year | Rival, supplier and paymaster | [S29][S31] |

**The most dangerous competitor is Samsung**, because it sells Apple the scarce input. Its record Q2 2026 operating profit of KRW89.5tn [S35] was earned largely in memory while the handset market shrank 22% [S30]: margin transferred from Apple's product P&L to its supplier. Apple's 10-Q warns memory costs will "intensify" [S6], so FY2027 gross margin is the line to underwrite.

**In China, Huawei is the dangerous one:** 21.3% of Q3 2026 shipments to Apple's 19.5% on Counterpoint's count, shipments up 19% while the market fell 10% [S39]; IDC has 21.1% to 17.8% on a 15.4% fall [S38]. Its premium-segment share is not disclosed in retrieved sources — the number that separates share loss from mix loss.

Alphabet is rival, supplier and paymaster: Siri runs on Gemini [S29] while Google pays $20bn a year for default search [S31].

The "do nothing" substitute is winning: a 22% unit decline means consumers keep handsets longer [S30], and Apple answers with price, not volume — iPhone revenue +22% on units -4% [S6][S30]. That holds only while rivals' costs rise too, so normalising memory would reverse the mix gain [S36].

**Is the premium widening?**
Yes: gross margin 44.1% in FY2023, 46.2% in FY2024, 46.9% in FY2025 [S1], then 50.1% in the June 2026 quarter [S6]. Peers read the same way — Xiaomi at 19.8% overall and 8.5% on phones [S36], Microsoft's gross-margin percentage falling on AI infrastructure [S33], Samsung's profit memory-driven [S35]. Apple defends it through mix (Services at 75.4% [S1]) and purchasing scale, not unit growth.

Counter-evidence, labelled: part of the premium is bought. Tariff refunds and favourable mix, not pricing, lifted the June-quarter products margin [S6], and 350% memory inflation is a cost Apple cannot control while Samsung earns record profit from it [S35]. Regulation attacks the 75.4% margin directly: the EU fined Apple EUR 500m [S16] and cut the standard commission to 26%, with 15% on link-out, from 1 October 2026 [S32]. Omdia adds that AI is not yet driving purchases [S30].

**Durability.** Switching costs hold: 2.5bn active devices [S28] and a 75.4% Services margin [S1]. What is being competed away is the take rate; watch Services growth excluding App Store commission, which Apple does not disclose.

**For an investor, the moat holds on switching costs while the premium is borrowed from a memory cycle: pay for the annuity, not the margin.**

**Confidence: medium, because shipment data are preliminary and IDC, Counterpoint and Omdia disagree by up to 5pp on China's decline [S38][S39], Samsung's handset-only profitability is not disclosed, the dollar split is Q1 not Q3 [S37], and Apple publishes no Services split.**"}],"isError":false}

Q4 FY2026 is guided to 47–48% from 50.1% [S17][S24], and each 100bp is 3.0% of trailing EPS, so the guide is 6–9% of annual earnings [S6].

3. **Multiple de-rating — medium/high, first test 2 November 2026.** 39.4x against FY2022–FY2025 year-ends of 24.6–37.5x [S7] and a Microsoft/Alphabet median of 22.0x [S9][S11], with the 10-year at 5.04% [S14]: 28.0x costs 29% and 22.0x costs 44% [S7].

Apple's franchise risk is modest; the priced risk is severe. At 39.4x trailing earnings [S7] the shares have no room for a memory-cost cycle and a European take-rate reset that have both begun [S30][S32].

**Seven risks, ranked by probability and impact**

1. **Memory-cost margin reset — high/high, into FY2027.** Memory costs are up 350% year on year [S30] and the 10-Q expects NAND/DRAM constraints to intensify [S6]. Q4 FY2026 is guided to 47–48% from 50.1% [S17][S24], and each 100bp is 3.0% of trailing EPS, so the guide is 6–9% of annual earnings [S6].

2. **Services take-rate reset — high/high, live since 1 October 2026.** The European Commission fined Apple EUR 500m on 23 April 2025 [S16]; commissions are now 26% in-app, 20% on alternative payment, 15% on link-out, plus a 5% Core Technology Commission [S32]. That taxes the 75.4%-margin line that is 26.2% of revenue, and no Services split lets filings size it [S1].

3. **Multiple de-rating — medium/high, first test 2 November 2026.** 39.4x against FY2022–FY2025 year-ends of 24.6–37.5x [S7], a Microsoft/Alphabet median of 22.0x [S9][S11] and a 5.04% ten-year [S14]: 28.0x on trailing EPS costs 29% and 22.0x costs 44% [S7].

4. **China unit erosion under a rebounding revenue line — medium/medium, FY2027.** China shipments fell 15.4% in calendar Q3 2026 and Apple's units 4.3%, share rising to 17.8% from 15.8% [S18], while Greater China revenue rose 30% to $64.8bn in nine months on renminbi strength and Pro mix [S6].

5. **iPhone cycle mean reversion — medium/high, FY2027.** iPhone is 53.9% of nine-month revenue [S6] and grew 22% in the June 2026 quarter after 0% in FY2024 and 4% in FY2025 [S1].

6. **Dependence on a competitor — high/medium.** Siri runs on Gemini under a non-exclusive agreement of 12 January 2026 [S29], while Google pays $20bn a year to be the default search engine with exclusivity banned [S31]; a cut to those payments would remove a material, undisclosed share of Services profit [S1].

7. **Trade policy — medium/medium, live.** Section 232 added no tariffs on Apple products in January 2026 and the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs in February, but new Section 301 duties have since been imposed and the refunds that flattered the June quarter do not repeat [S6][S17].

**The strongest case against the thesis.** The watchlist assumes a de-rating that may never come. Apple's 2.7% free-cash-flow yield is the highest of the peer set (Microsoft 1.5%, Alphabet 1.3%) [S7][S9][S11], its 10.6x EV/Sales is below Microsoft's 11.3x despite a higher gross margin [S7][S9][S1], and $82.2bn of buybacks shrink the count [S6]. A fund that waits for $305 can miss years of that compounding.

**Stress tests.** Revenue 30% lower cuts EPS 30% to $6.10 on $466.8bn of trailing revenue [S6], which at 39.4x is $240 [S7] — at the $241 bear case, moving the rating to Hold-off until a replacement-cycle trough is visible. Multiple compressed: 28.0x gives −29% and 22.0x −44% [S7][S9][S11], $193–244 on trailing EPS with margins intact, through the $305 entry — the watchlist converts the biggest risk into the entry point. Free cash flow 30% lower takes $136.7bn to $95.7bn [S6], EV/FCF to 51.8x and the yield to 1.9% [S7]; at a 2.7% yield the equity is worth $3.54tn, 29% below the $5.02tn capitalisation.

[risk matrix table unchanged]

**What this means for the investor.** No risk is fatal alone, but three point the same way, into the same quarter. The position stays at zero until the 2 November 2026 print shows whether the margin step-down is an input-cost cycle or a reset [S15].

**Confidence: medium, because** the filing evidence is strong — the memory warning sits in the 10-Q [S6], the fee schedule in the European Commission's record [S16][S32] — but the two largest risks, memory prices and EU remedies, sit outside Apple's control and cannot be quantified from its disclosures [S1].

Apple's franchise risk is modest; the priced risk is severe. At 39.4x trailing earnings [S7] the shares have no room for a memory-cost cycle and a European take-rate reset that have both begun [S30][S32].

That taxes the 75.4%-margin line that is 26.2% of revenue, and no Services split lets filings size it [S1].

3. **Multiple de-rating — medium/high, first test 2 November 2026.** 39.4x against FY2022–FY2025 year-ends of 24.6–37.5x [S7], a Microsoft/Alphabet median of 22.0x [S9][S11] and a 5.04% ten-year [S14]: 28.0x on trailing EPS costs 29% and 22.0x costs 44% [S7].

4. **China unit erosion under a rebounding revenue line — medium/medium, FY2027.** China shipments fell 15.4% in calendar Q3 2026 and Apple's units 4.3%, share rising to 17.8% from 15.8% [S18], while Greater China revenue rose 30% to $64.8bn in nine months on renminbi strength and Pro mix [S6].

5. **iPhone cycle mean reversion — medium/high, FY2027.** iPhone is 53.9% of nine-month revenue [S6] and grew 22% in the June 2026 quarter after 0% in FY2024 and 4% in FY2025 [S1].

6. **Dependence on a competitor — high/medium.** Siri runs on Gemini under a non-exclusive agreement of 12 January 2026 [S29] while Google pays $20bn a year for default search with exclusivity banned [S31]; a cut to those payments would remove a material, undisclosed share of Services profit [S1].

7. **Trade policy — medium/medium, live.** Section 232 added no tariffs on Apple products in January 2026 and the Supreme Court struck down certain IEEPA tariffs in February, but new Section 301 duties have since been imposed and the refunds that flattered the June quarter do not repeat [S6][S17].

The scenario work argues for a watchlist, not a position: the probability-weighted value is $322, 6% below the 28 October 2026 close of $343.83, and the best case returns 14% only if the multiple holds [S6][S7][S24]. FY2027 gross margin decides most of the outcome and gets its first dated test on 2 November 2026 [S15][S24].

**Bull — 25%, $392, +14%.** Revenue +11% to $523.1bn, gross margin 48.5%, EPS $10.45 and the multiple holds 37.5x, Apple's FY2024 year-end [S6][S7]. Memory prices normalise, Services compounds 13% at a 75.4% margin [S1], and Gemini-powered Siri drives a replacement cycle [S29]. Signposts: margin at or above 48% on 2 November [S15][S24]; memory spot prices falling [S30]; China units stabilising [S18].

**Base — 50%, $327, −5%.** Revenue +8% to $509.0bn, gross margin 47.7% in line with the Q4 guide, EPS $9.90 and the multiple holds 33.0x — 16% below today's 39.4x, below the FY2024 37.5x and FY2025 34.2x year-ends and 6% above the 31.1x four-year median [S7][S24]; that premium pays for a 2.7% free-cash-flow yield against 1.5% at Microsoft and 1.3% at Alphabet [S7][S9][S11]. At Microsoft's 27.7x the same $9.90 is $274, at the 22.0x median $218 [S9][S11].

**Bear — 25%, $241, −30%.** Revenue +2% to $480.7bn, memory costs hold gross margin at 46.5%, the EU remedy trims the Services take rate [S32] and the multiple de-rates to 28.0x, the FY2023 year-end, on EPS of $8.62 [S6][S7]. Signposts: a Q4 miss against the 47–48% guide [S24]; EU periodic penalties [S16]; China units falling faster than share rises [S18].

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bull | 25% | +11% revenue, 48.5% margin, 37.5x | $392, +14% | Margin ≥48% on 2 Nov; memory falling | [S1][S7][S24][S29][S30] |
| Base | 50% | +8% revenue, 47.7% margin, 33.0x | $327, −5% | China holds; buybacks near $82bn | [S6][S9][S11][S24] |
| Bear | 25% | +2% revenue, 46.5% margin, 28.0x | $241, −30% | Q4 margin below 47%; EU penalties; China units | [S16][S18][S24][S32] |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 4 | Share count | 14.72bn / 14.42bn | 1.6% of EPS, about $5 a share | Buyback pace, $82.2bn | [S6] |
| 5 | Services take rate | not disclosed | Unquantified; the bear's margin risk | EU fee schedule; DOJ case | [S32][S34] |

The multiple is the largest swing and the one we cannot test; the margin has a date on it, which is why entry is gated on the print, not the price alone [S15].

1. **Quality is not the question.** Services is 26.2% of FY2025 revenue at a 75.4% gross margin and trailing free cash flow is $136.7bn at 1.06x conversion [S1][S6]; this is a business we want to own at some price.

**The most dangerous competitor is Samsung**, because it sells Apple the scarce input. Its record Q2 2026 operating profit of KRW89.5tn [S35] was earned largely in memory while the handset market shrank 22% [S30]: margin transferred from Apple's product P&L to its supplier. The scenario work argues for a watchlist, not a position: the probability-weighted value is $322, 6% below the 28 October 2026 close of $343.83, and the best case returns 14% only if the multiple holds [S6][S7][S24].
